items.title: Citing loss-of-control risk, EASA orders additional ATR de-icing system checks
items.summary:
The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) has ordered operators of ATR 42 and ATR 72 turboprops to check their de-icing systems as often as every 160 flight hours, warning that a valve failure could go undetected until an aircraft encounters icing and lead to an unrecoverable loss of control.

The airworthiness directive, issued November 16, 2026, takes effect November 30. EASA had already shortened the time between checks in January 2025 after a design review identified the risk. A subsequent analysis of how the valves could fail prompted ATR to revise its maintenance instructions again in October.

Brazilian investigators identified ice buildup and multiple de-icing system failures among the factors that contributed to the August 9, 2024, crash of Voepass Flight 2283 . All 62 people aboard the ATR 72-500 died when it crashed in Vinhedo, Brazil. ATR issued its first notice to operators about the valve checks in October 2024, about two months after the accident.

The order covers the valves that regulate pressure and shut off the air supply to the de-icing system. How often operators must test them depends on the aircraft model and whether ATR modified it at the factory or an operator had the work done later.

The biggest change is for modified ATR 42-400s, ATR 42-500s and ATR 72s. Under the January 2025 order, those aircraft could fly up to 1,050 hours between checks. The new limit is 160 hours, an 85% reduction. For aircraft of the same models without the modification, the interval drops from 700 hours to 210. Operators of the earlier ATR 42-200, -300 and -320…
items.t: Citing loss-of-control risk, EASA orders additional ATR de-icing system checks

items.title: Azul puts its first Cessna SkyCourier to work flying oil crews in the Amazon
items.summary:
Azul Conecta has put its first Cessna SkyCourier to work flying oil crews for Petrobras in the Brazilian Amazon. The regional airline also plans to sell seats on the weekly flights that bring the 19-seat turboprop back to Manaus and return it to the oilfields.

The aircraft, registered PS-ENE, arrived in Brazil recently and entered service on November 3, 2026. Azul won a four-year contract to transport workers for the Brazilian oil company, whose operations in the state of Amazonas include the oil and gas fields at Porto Urucu.

Under the schedule Azul outlined to CNN Brasil , the SkyCourier will leave Carauari on Fridays, stop in Coari and continue to Manaus, the state capital. On Mondays, it will fly the route in reverse. Passengers can buy seats on those flights even if they have no connection to Petrobras.

With 19 seats, the twin-engine SkyCourier can carry more than twice as many passengers as Azul Conecta’s nine-seat Cessna Grand Caravans. Chief Executive Vitor Cordeiro told Brazilian outlet UOL that several of the airline’s regional routes have outgrown the Caravan but still draw too few passengers to warrant an ATR 72. The Petrobras contract helped make the purchase possible.

Azul Conecta expects its second SkyCourier in the first half of 2027. One destination Cordeiro is considering is Barcelos, an Amazon fishing town the airline already serves by Caravan.

For passengers heading there, the appeal of the larger Cessna may be in the baggage hold. Anglers often bring bulky tackle along with their luggage, and space aboard the Caravan is limited.

Azul has yet to…
items.t: Azul puts its first Cessna SkyCourier to work flying oil crews in the Amazon

items.title: Here's How The Boeing 757-300 Protects Its Ultra-Long Fuselage On Rotation In The Cockpit & Externally
items.summary: At 178 feet, seven inches (54.43 meters), the Boeing 757-300 is the longest single-aisle twinjet ever built. Yet its extra length created an unexpected engineering challenge that had little to do with seats, range, landing gear, or engines. It was the runway . Boeing stretched the 757-200 by 23 feet, four inches (7.11 meters), and every extra foot behind the main landing gear increased the distance between the aircraft's pivot point and its tail, making ground clearance during rotation a critical consideration.
items.t: Here's How The Boeing 757-300 Protects Its Ultra-Long Fuselage On Rotation In The Cockpit & Externally

items.title: FAA investigates how a router upgrade in Arkansas led to US ground stop
items.summary:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is investigating how a routine router replacement at a radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas, disrupted communications at 17 of its 22 en route air traffic control centers on November 13, 2026, forcing the agency to halt departures across the US for more than four hours.

A central question the investigation is now focused on is why a different router in Amarillo, Texas, also began wreaking havoc on the system, despite the sites being more than 500 miles apart. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the router there began flooding the same network with data when L3Harris switched on the new unit in Arkansas. The contractor had completed its work in Texas three weeks earlier.

L3Harris, which owns and operates the FAA’s telecommunications network, was moving the El Dorado site from copper wire to fiber. The work involved installing a Juniper Networks router to replace an older Cisco unit. Duffy said the contractor had performed similar work thousands of times.

At about 3:30 p.m. Eastern time, the FAA began seeing problems with radio communications and radar feeds. Its network was receiving about 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds. The disruption spread beyond the en route centers to several terminal radar approach control facilities, which handle arriving and departing aircraft at larger airports.

Some radio frequencies and radar feeds remained available, and controllers used them to guide about 3,500 airborne aircraft to safe landings. Medical, law enforcement and military flights were allowed to continue.…
items.t: FAA investigates how a router upgrade in Arkansas led to US ground stop

items.title: Estonia blames Russian GRU for arson plot targeting drone maker Threod Systems
items.summary:
Estonian authorities have detained eight suspects following an attempted arson attack on drone manufacturer Threod Systems, which the country’s Internal Security Service (KAPO) attributes to Russia’s military intelligence agency, the GRU. 

The attack took place at 03:06 local time on November 14, 2026, at the company’s facility in Viimsi, near Tallinn, the Estonian Prosecutor’s Office said in a statement published on November 15, 2026 . The attackers intended to cause an explosion and set the building on fire. 

Threod Systems suffered no significant damage, thanks to “the company’s preparedness and the quick response of a security guard”, according to prosecutors. 

Founded in 2012, Threod Systems develops and manufactures unmanned aircraft systems for military surveillance, reconnaissance, and target acquisition. Its products include the Eos C and Eos D vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) drones, electro-optical sensor systems, and launchers for one-way attack drones. According to the company, it has delivered its equipment to 27 countries, including 14 NATO members and Ukraine.

The Estonian government said separately that no one was injured and that the company’s production and deliveries were unaffected. 

Estonian intelligence attributes attack to Russia’s GRU  

KAPO and the Police and Border Guard Board detained eight suspects, five of whom prosecutors have asked a court to remand in custody. 

Prosecutor General Astrid Asi said the case is being investigated under a provision of Estonia’s Penal Code covering acts against national security carried out on behalf of…
items.t: Estonia blames Russian GRU for arson plot targeting drone maker Threod Systems

The airline currently operates 20 A350-900 widebodies and has a further ten on order, according to ch-aviation data.

China Southern 

“Inspired by modern aesthetics, the all-new cabin combines refined design, ergonomic features and ambient lighting to enhance comfort and functionality on long-haul flights,” China southern said.

Thompson Aero Seating announced in April 2025 that China Southern would be the first customer of its new VantageXL+, the latest evolution of its VantageXL product.

According to Thomson, it will deliver 18 business-class seats per aircraft in a 1-2-1 LOPA configuration. Each will have a minimum seat width of 24” and a bed length of 76.9” at a 44” pitch.

Each A350 will also include an enhanced front row creating a first-class experience and accommodating four passengers. The bed length in the front row is 80.8” and features companion seats with dropping dividers.

“Vantage XL+ is the latest generation product, optimised specifically for next generation widebody aircraft based on our highly acclaimed Vantage XL platform,” Andy Morris, CCO of Thompson Aero Seating, said. “It delivers…

items.title: ASELSAN signs contracts to supply missile seekers, data links to ROKETSAN
items.summary:
Turkish defense electronics manufacturer ASELSAN has signed contracts worth a combined €1.28 billion ($1.41 billion) with missile manufacturer ROKETSAN to supply missile data link and seeker systems. 

ASELSAN disclosed the agreements in a filing with Turkey’s Public Disclosure Platform (KAP) on November 16, 2026. The filing identifies ROKETSAN as the customer but does not name the missile programs involved, quantities ordered, or delivery schedule. 

ROKETSAN produces a range of missiles and air-launched precision-guided munitions, including the MAM family , although the filing does not indicate whether these weapons are covered by the contracts. Missile seekers detect and track targets, typically during the final phase of flight, while data links allow targeting information to be updated after launch. 

According to the disclosure, ROKETSAN accounted for 5.6% of ASELSAN’s net sales in its latest published financial statements and 7.3% of its trade receivables. 

ASELSAN builds on earlier ROKETSAN deal 

The announcement follows another major agreement between the two Turkish defense companies. On September 23, 2026, ASELSAN disclosed a €1.23 billion ($1.36 billion) contract to supply ROKETSAN with subsystems for air defense systems. 

ASELSAN has also announced several large contracts with Turkey’s Presidency of Defense Industries (SSB) in recent weeks. On October 5, 2026, it reported agreements worth €2.46 billion ($2.71 billion) for hybrid air defense systems. On October 26, 2026, it disclosed a further €523 million ($576 million) contract to develop a new-generation…
items.t: ASELSAN signs contracts to supply missile seekers, data links to ROKETSAN

items.title: Widerøe to receive new Embraer E195-E2 aircraft early 2028

In 2018, Widerøe became the world’s first operator of the Embraer E2 aircraft family when the airline introduced its first three E190-E2 aircraft.

Markus Mainka / Shutterstock.com 

According to Widerøe, since acquiring its first three E190-E2 aircraft, they have tripled the number of passengers flying between Bergen and Tromsø.

“This investment is a direct response to the trust that Norwegian passengers and local communities place in us every single day,” Jenssen added. “With Norwegian’s support, Widerøe can continue developing critical infrastructure and air routes throughout Norway.”

The carrier has deployed its Embraer E190-E2s on both domestic and international routes. Widerøe’s international destinations include Ireland, Scotland, Sweden, Italy and France.

Widerøe said it has been “very satisfied with the operational reliability and performance” of its Embraer jets.

“The new aircraft will contribute to further operational efficiencies…
items.t: Widerøe to receive new Embraer E195-E2 aircraft early 2028

items.title: Philippine Airlines firms order for up to 20 Boeing 787-10s with GE engines
items.summary:
Philippine Airlines (PAL) has signed firm contracts with Boeing and GE Aerospace for up to 20 Boeing 787-10 Dreamliners, converting a commitment first announced at the Farnborough International Airshow in July 2026 into a confirmed order.

The agreements, covering the aircraft and their GEnx-1B engines, were signed on November 10, 2026, and announced by the airline on November 15.

The order is central to the flag carrier’s plans to renew and expand its long-haul fleet.

15 firm 787-10s, options for five more, deliveries next decade 

The contracts cover 15 firm Boeing 787-10s, with purchase rights for five more. 

All will be powered by GE Aerospace’s GEnx-1B engines. Deliveries are scheduled for the next decade, though the airline did not give a more precise timeline.

The value of the order and the delivery schedule were not disclosed. PAL also did not say which routes the aircraft will fly, or whether they will replace existing aircraft or add to the fleet.

PAL bets on capacity and fuel efficiency for long-haul growth 

PAL Holdings President and Chief Operating Officer Lucio C. Tan III said the aircraft would play “an important role” in the airline’s plans to modernize and expand its fleet. He pointed to the type’s passenger capacity and fuel efficiency as the main reasons for the choice.

“As we look at our network and the markets we want to serve, we see considerable opportunities for growth,” Tan said. 

He added that having the right aircraft and engines was essential to offering passengers more choice and better connections.

Boeing and GE Aerospace see wider…
items.t: Philippine Airlines firms order for up to 20 Boeing 787-10s with GE engines

items.title: Suspected GPS jamming affects 80 aircraft, disrupts Schiphol approaches
items.summary:
Dozens of aircraft flying over the Netherlands and neighboring countries experienced GPS interference on the evening of November 9, 2026. Seven flights approaching Amsterdam Schiphol Airport (AMS) encountered problems with satellite-based navigation, according to Dutch air traffic control. 

A spokesperson for Air Traffic Control the Netherlands (LVNL) told Dutch newspaper NRC , which first reported the incident on November 15, 2026, that Required Navigation Performance (RNP) approaches at Schiphol were disrupted. The spokesperson said deliberate GPS interference, known as jamming, was a plausible cause. 

All seven aircraft landed safely with assistance from air traffic controllers. LVNL said the disruption had no consequences for flight safety. 

GPS interference affects around 80 aircraft 

The interference extended well beyond Schiphol. Analysis of aircraft tracking data cited by Belgian public broadcaster VRT NWS suggests that around 80 aircraft experienced degraded satellite navigation over the Netherlands, Belgium, eastern England and northwestern Germany, most of them at high altitude. 

US data analyst John Wiseman, creator of the GPSJAM interference map, reconstructed the incident using aircraft tracking data. He placed the disruption between 18:08 and 18:27 local time. 

Wiseman’s analysis identified a possible interference source in the North Sea, around 80 to 110 nautical miles (148 to 204 kilometers, or 92 to 127 miles) north of the Dutch island of Texel. The estimated altitude was consistent with a transmitter aboard a ship, although Wiseman cautioned that…
items.t: Suspected GPS jamming affects 80 aircraft, disrupts Schiphol approaches

items.title: ULA rocket fails after liftoff with 40 Amazon Leo satellites destroyed
items.summary:
A United Launch Alliance (ULA) rocket failed 10 minutes after liftoff while transporting 40 Amazon Leo satellites into low Earth orbit.

On November 15, 2026, the ULA Vulcan VC6L rocket launched from Space Launch Complex-41 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida, but “suffered an anomaly” several minutes into the flight.

The mission was the first of 38 Vulcan rocket launches for Amazon to expand its satellite constellation following ULA’s eight successful deployment missions using Atlas V.

ULA said it will work with Amazon and other appropriate organizations to “find the cause, determine the appropriate corrective action, and return to flight as quickly as possible”.

“Every flight generates data, and every flight teaches us something,” ULA said shortly after the failed mission. “Since the anomaly just occurred, we don’t have any specific data yet to understand what occurred today. ULA exists to provide assured access to space for our nation and for the customers who depend on us. That purpose is why we take on some of the hardest missions in spaceflight, and why we hold ourselves to the standard of mission success. Today, we did not meet that standard.”

Once over 3,000 Amazon Leo satellites are positioned in low Earth orbit, they will provide high-speed, low-latency internet access virtually anywhere in the world and become a direct competitor to Elon Musk’s Starlink.

“There is risk with any launch, and that’s especially true for inaugural missions like LV-01,” Amazon said. “ULA has been a trusted partner for Amazon, and we believe they’ll learn from this…
items.t: ULA rocket fails after liftoff with 40 Amazon Leo satellites destroyed

items.title: South Korean government approves merger between three low-cost airlines
items.summary:
The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport of South Korea has approved a three-way merger between low-cost carriers Air Seoul, Air Busan, and Jin Air to form a single operator. 

This consolidation is a consequence of Korean Air’s acquisition of Asiana Airlines to form a single national airline. The merger between South Korea’s two largest airlines is expected to be formally completed on December 17, 2026 . 

Replicating the move made by their respective parent companies, Jin Air, which is a subsidiary of Korean Air, will merge with Air Seoul and Air Busan, which belong to Asiana Airlines. 

The resulting carrier, which will use the Jin Air brand, will start operating as an integrated entity from March 17, 2027. 

The merger has already been cleared by the Fair Trade Commission (FTC), Korea’s competition authority, so the only remaining formal step before completion is shareholder approval, which is slated for December 2026. 

According to ch-aviation data, the three airlines have a combined fleet of 58 active aircraft. Jin Air has 31 active aircraft (plus another three listed as inactive), including three Boeing 777s, one Airbus A321, seven B737 MAX 8s, 18 B737-800s and two B737-900s. In turn, Air Busan operates 21 aircraft, all from the A320 family, while Air Seoul operates six A321s. 

According to reports in Korean media, the integration of Air Busan is a particularly sensitive part of the project. Officials in Busan, Korea’s second-largest city, fear the city will lose out because of the merger and have asked for the new airline to be headquartered there.…
items.t: South Korean government approves merger between three low-cost airlines

items.title: US Air Force’s first overseas-based F-15EX fighters arrive in Japan
items.summary:
Two F-15EX Eagle II fighters assigned to the 67th Fighter Squadron landed at Kadena Air Base (DNA) in Okinawa, Japan, on November 15, 2026, becoming the first of the type to be permanently stationed overseas.

Kadena is the first overseas US Air Force installation to receive combat-coded F-15EX aircraft. It is also the second US Air Force location to field the fighter, after the Oregon Air National Guard’s 142nd Wing at Portland Air National Guard Base, which received its first operational F-15EX in June 2024 .

F-15EX begins replacing Kadena’s aging Eagle fleet 

Two US Air Force F-15EX Eagle II fighters from the 67th Fighter Squadron approach Kadena Air Base, Japan. (Credit: U.S. Air Force photo) 

The arrival marks the next phase in replacing Kadena’s F-15C/D Eagles, whose phased withdrawal began in November 2022 after more than four decades of service at the base. In the interim, rotational deployments of fourth- and fifth-generation fighters maintained a continuous fighter presence on Okinawa.

Under a plan announced in July 2024 , the US Air Force intends to station 36 F-15EX aircraft at Kadena. Both of the wing’s fighter squadrons, the 44th and the 67th, will operate the type. The November 2026 release gave no timeline for the remaining deliveries, describing the arrival as part of a phased transition that will continue as additional aircraft enter service.

The F-15EX brings upgraded avionics, electronic warfare systems, and greater weapons-carrying capacity than its predecessors. The aircraft is intended to strengthen Kadena’s air defense capabilities while…
items.t: US Air Force’s first overseas-based F-15EX fighters arrive in Japan

items.title: Spanish airline Plus Ultra files for creditor protection, drops routes
items.summary:
Spanish long-haul carrier Plus Ultra Líneas Aéreas is preparing to implement a thorough restructuring after filing for preliminary creditor protection on November 13, 2026. The airline will now have three months, extendable by another three, to agree a restructuring plan with its creditors.

According to several Spanish media outlets, Plus Ultra will stop all scheduled operations outside the ones currently linking Caracas (CCS) to Madrid-Barajas (MAD) and Tenerife-North (TFN), in the Canary Islands. The carrier also plans to orient most of its activity towards the ACMI market , leasing its aircraft to other operators. 

Plus Ultra’s workforce is also expected to undergo significant cuts, which according to Spanish media will affect most of its approximately 670 members of staff. 

As of November 2026, Plus Ultra operates a fleet of seven Airbus A330 widebody aircraft (five -200s and two -300s) from its hub in Madrid. Until now, its network focused mostly on Latin American destinations, such as Lima (LIM), Buenos Aires (EZE) and the aforementioned Caracas. Service to Cartagena de Indias (CTG), Colombia, had already been suspended in June 2026.

The airline has blamed the hike in fuel prices resulting from the military conflict in the Middle East for its challenging financial situation. In this regard, the airline has linked its decision to keep only its regular service to Venezuela to the fact that it can source cheaper fuel in that South American country. 

This adverse cost environment adds to an already fragile financial situation, the result of several years of…
items.t: Spanish airline Plus Ultra files for creditor protection, drops routes

items.title: A B737 and a B767 collide on the ground at Miami International Airport
items.summary:
Two aircraft, a Copa Airlines B737-800 and a B767 freighter operated by UPS, collided on the ground at Miami International Airport (MIA), Florida, on the night of November 14, 2026. 

The incident happened at around 21.15 local time when the B737, which had just landed and was taxiing to the gate, sliced through the nose of the B767 with its left wingtip, as the latter was preparing to take off.

Copa Airlines flight 427 had just landed from Panama City (PTY) with 166 passengers and six crew members onboard, while UPS flight 358 was preparing to take off for Bogota (BOG), Colombia. 

The Panamanian airline stated that two passengers that were traveling onboard its aircraft suffered minor injuries in the collision, although none required hospitalization. 

Air traffic control (ATC) audio that has since been made public shows the B767 had been instructed to give way to the taxiing B737. However, for reasons yet to be determined, it went too far ahead, and its nose entered the area where the other aircraft was moving. 

Passengers onboard the Copa flight recorded on their mobile phones the aftermath of the collision as seen from inside the aircraft, with footage since having been posted on social media. Pictures taken after the incident show significant damage on the nose of the freighter.

The mishap happened as airports and airlines across the United States were still recovering from a nationwide ground stop the day before. The nationwide outage, which lasted approximately four hours, has been attributed to technical issues with air traffic control equipment.

The post A…
items.t: A B737 and a B767 collide on the ground at Miami International Airport

items.title: SpaceX successfully recovers Starship upper stage in world first
items.summary:
SpaceX achieved another industry first on November 14, 2026, as it successfully recovered the upper stage of a Starship rocket.

While Elon Musk’s firm had so far managed to regularly recover the booster stages of the rockets it launches, this is the first time ever that the upper stage makes it safely to the ground after an orbital flight.

Recovering the upper stage is much harder than recovering the booster. The upper stage flies higher and much faster to reach orbit, and has to shed that speed on the way back, generating enormous amounts of heat during reentry.

This milestone opens the door to fully reusing Starship in future missions, potentially lowering the cost of access to space dramatically. NASA, for example, expects to use Starship for its return to the Moon, with a crewed landing planned for 2028 .

This particular Starship launched on November 13, 2026, on the Starship program’s 15th test flight and the fourth with its V3 version (and the second of them to reach orbit ). After spending 22 and a half hours in orbit and deploying 26 Starlink satellites, it returned to Earth, landing at Starbase Texas, where the upper stage was caught by a pair of mechanical arms. 

The Super Heavy booster stage of this same rocket was expected to be caught the same way, but it finally splashe d down in the ocean due to a technical issue.

The post SpaceX successfully recovers Starship upper stage in world first appeared first on AeroTime .
items.t: SpaceX successfully recovers Starship upper stage in world first

items.title: China’s COMAC completes first piloted flight of CE-25A electric aircraft
items.summary:
China’s first domestically developed fixed-wing electric commercial aircraft, the CE-25A, completed its first piloted test flight on November 14, 2026.

The aircraft took off and landed in Binzhou, in Shandong province, southeast of Beijing, with two pilots and a flight test engineer on board. It spent 16 minutes and 38 seconds in the air and covered 37.5 miles (60.4 kilometers). The entire test, including ground operations, lasted 57 minutes and 46 seconds. 

Chinese news agency China News Service has posted a video of the test flight online.

Developed by state-owned aerospace manufacturer COMAC, the CE-25A has a maximum takeoff weight of 10 metric tons and is designed to carry up to 19 passengers plus crew. It is powered by 10 electric ducted fans, mounted five-abreast on each wing. COMAC expects it to have a range of around 250 miles (400 kilometers) and a cruise speed of 186 mph (300 km/h). 

COMAC unveiled the CE-25A concept in 2023, but the first public images of a full-size aircraft only emerged in October 2026 , triggering speculation about the program’s status. 

According to Chinese state media, the aircraft had in fact been flying for months, with 19 unmanned flights completed since February 2, 2026. 

Chinese battery giant CATL is COMAC’s main industrial partner in the project, alongside Shanghai Jiao Tong University. 

The battery maker, which already has a strong lead in the global electric vehicle market, is also making inroads into aviation. CATL is a strategic investor in Chinese eVTOL developer AutoFlight and, at the 2023 Shanghai auto show, unveiled a…

items.title: Duffy presses Republican Congress to fund ATC overhaul after nationwide outage
items.summary:
As US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy faces the prospect of hours of congressional grilling over what precisely caused a massive outage of the country’s air traffic control system on November 13, 2026, he used a White House press conference to lay at least some of the blame on a Republican-led Congress he said had yet to provide the money needed to modernize the system.

“How many times does this have to happen before Congress gives the money to fix it?” Duffy asked.

By the time Duffy spoke, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) had lifted a nationwide ground stop that halted most US departures for more than four hours. Duffy told reporters the agency needs $50 billion to overhaul the ATC system. Just that morning, before the first reports of trouble with the ATC system surfaced in Chicago, Duffy and White House budget director Russell Vought had asked lawmakers for $30.1 billion for air traffic control and airport upgrades.

Lawmakers approved $12.5 billion in July 2025 for ATC upgrades and controller hiring, including $1.9 billion to replace outdated en route centers. The Republican majority on the Senate Commerce Committee said Friday’s outage showed why the FAA should give those centers priority. Sen. Maria Cantwell of Washington, the committee’s ranking Democrat, said the panel was looking into the telecommunications problems.

The request that morning included $10.1 billion for ATC modernization, $2 billion for control towers and $18 billion for airport projects. Of the airport money, $10 billion would go toward modernizing or replacing aging terminals. At…
items.t: Duffy presses Republican Congress to fund ATC overhaul after nationwide outage

items.title: FAA halts all US departures, warns airborne flights to expect holding nationwide
items.summary:
The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop shortly before 4 p.m. Eastern time on November 13, 2026, after a communications outage affected every US Air Route Traffic Control Center (ARTCC) in the country. It was the first time since January 2023 that the agency had halted departures nationwide, and only the second nationwide ground stop since the 9/11 terror attacks in 2001.

The FAA subsequently advised crews to expect airborne holding at airports nationwide because of equipment outages. Flightradar24 reported that about 3,100 aircraft were airborne and bound for US airports during the ground stop. The tracking figure includes all US-bound flights in the air at the time. The number actually holding was unclear.

US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy described the problem as “a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers” and said FAA technicians were investigating. The regional centers direct aircraft primarily during the en route portion of a flight. Duffy’s initial statement did not identify which system had failed or give a time for departures to resume.

The nationwide order followed an earlier halt in Chicago, where air traffic controllers had encountered communications problems. Houston’s George Bush Intercontinental Airport (IAH) subsequently confirmed it was holding all departures. At San Francisco International Airport (SFO), spokesman Doug Yakel said aircraft already en route continued to land while departures were held.

The previous nationwide ground stop, on January 11, 2023, lasted roughly 90…
items.t: BREAKING: FAA halts all US departures, warns airborne flights to expect holding nationwide

items.title: US airlines brace for busiest travel day since pandemic amid Thanksgiving rush
items.summary:
US airlines expect to carry nearly 29 million passengers over the 2026 Thanksgiving travel weekend, with the biggest crowds due as travelers head home from family celebrations.

American Airlines has scheduled 7,021 flights for November 29, its busiest day since the pandemic, while United said it expects about 600,000 passengers that day.

Airlines for America expects November 29 and 30 to be the two busiest days of the 11-day period that begins November 20. US carriers are offering an average of 38,000 more seats per day than they did over Thanksgiving last year, according to the trade group.

The Sunday after Thanksgiving in 2025 was the busiest day the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) had ever recorded. TSA screened more than 3.13 million people at US airports on November 30, more than twice the 1.56 million who passed through checkpoints on Thanksgiving Day. Nearly 2.9 million more passed through security on December 1.

Los Angeles International (LAX) handled the most checkpoint traffic during the seven days around Thanksgiving last year. About 689,000 people went through security at LAX, followed by 647,000 at New York’s John F. Kennedy International (JFK), 603,000 at Atlanta (ATL) and 598,000 at Chicago O’Hare (ORD), according to TSA figures.

American and its regional partners expect more than 8 million passengers across nearly 85,000 flights between November 19 and December 1. The schedule includes 4% more flights than last Thanksgiving.

At midday on November 29, American said it expects to have 1,130 flights in the air at once.

United expects to…
items.t: US airlines brace for busiest travel day since pandemic amid Thanksgiving rush

items.title: Quantum Systems says Bundeswehr drones flying again after cyberattack
items.summary:
On November 13, 2026, Quantum Systems announced that its drones operated by the Bundeswehr are flying again, after the German armed forces grounded them as a precaution following a cyberattack on the manufacturer.

“The fleet is operating normally around the globe, including Germany and the Bundeswehr,” a company spokesperson told Reuters in an emailed statement. “The Bundeswehr was the only customer to ground their systems as a precaution.”

Quantum Systems did not specify when the grounding began or ended, or how many drones were affected. The German military has not independently confirmed that flights have resumed. According to the Financial Times , the grounding prevented Quantum Systems from participating in a recent military exercise.

Cyberattack reportedly targeted Quantum Systems software updates 

In a statement published on November 12, 2026, Quantum Systems said that it had identified a cybersecurity incident at the end of October. An immediate internal investigation revealed “an active cyberattack by hostile actors,” the company claimed.

According to the German magazine Der Spiegel, the attackers placed a malicious file on a server used to distribute updates for QBase, Quantum Systems’ ground-control and mission-planning software. The company did not disclose these technical details in its public statement and nor did it identify the attackers.

Quantum Systems stressed that its IT and security teams contained the threat in cooperation with the authorities. It reported the incident to the relevant agencies, and an investigation remains underway with state…
items.t: Quantum Systems says Bundeswehr drones flying again after cyberattack

items.title: Saudi THC firms up 12-jet Bombardier order, with options for 48 more
items.summary:
Saudi Arabia’s The Helicopter Company (THC) has signed firm purchase agreements for 12 Bombardier business jets, turning a letter of intent announced at the Farnborough International Airshow in July 2026 into a binding order.

The deal, announced on November 13, 2026, covers five Challenger 3500s, five Global 5500s and two Global 8000s. Bombardier valued the order at approximately $568 million based on 2026 list prices.

The agreements also include options for another 48 aircraft across the three models, potentially bringing THC’s business jet fleet to 60 aircraft. Bombardier said THC has sole discretion over whether to exercise those options.

The manufacturer described the transaction as the largest business aviation fleet order to date in Saudi Arabia.

Saudi helicopter operator expands into business aviation 

THC is owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) and has been operating since mid-2019. Its fleet includes more than 60 helicopters used for emergency medical services, aerial work, private charter and tourism.

The Bombardier jets will be THC’s first fixed-wing aircraft. In the letter of intent in July 2026, the company said it planned to use the jets for charter and aircraft management services.

THC is also expanding its helicopter fleet. At Farnborough, it placed a firm order for eight additional Airbus H145 helicopters , scheduled for delivery in 2027 and 2028.

Captain Arnaud Martinez, Chief Executive Officer of THC, said the Bombardier agreement marks the company’s entry into business aviation, citing growing demand in Saudi Arabia and the wider…
items.t: Saudi THC firms up 12-jet Bombardier order, with options for 48 more

items.title: BA-owner IAG offers access to 122M travelers through new advertising firm
items.summary:
International Airlines Group (IAG), owner of British Airways and Iberia, is offering businesses and brands access to 122 million travelers a year through its new media and advertising firm.

On November 12, 2026, the company launched IAG Media, aiming to bring together advertising across all IAG airlines for the first time.

As well as the UK’s British Airways and Spain’s Iberia, IAG also owns Aer Lingus, Vueling and LEVEL.

With such an interlinked advertising framework, IAG believes it can use its scale, customer insights and growing onboard connectivity to help brands reach travelers at various points in their journey.

Lukas Wunderlich / Shutterstock 

This will include digital channels, such as in-flight entertainment and the Starlink Wi-Fi login portal, as well as advertising in airport lounges and inflight magazines.

Nacho Tovar, CEO of IAG Media, described travel as “one of the few moments when people are open to discovering new things,” and suggested that the new platform can “put brands right there with them”.

“It brings together the scale of more than 122 million customers with the breadth and diversity of our leading airline brands,” Tovar said. “Each of our airlines serve different customers and markets, giving us access to a highly diverse audience. By combining those insights with on-board connectivity, we can help brands reach customers with advertising that is much more relevant.”

Tovar added: “Our ambition is to build IAG Media into the leading travel media network.”

According to IAG, its strategy is to develop “capital-light, complementary…
items.t: BA-owner IAG offers access to 122M travelers through new advertising firm

items.title: SpiceJet flights from Dubai cancelled over unpaid airport fees: reports
items.summary:
Several SpiceJet flights from Dubai have been cancelled due to unpaid airport fees, according to reports shared by assorted Indian news websites.

On November 13, 2026, the Hindustan Times claimed that four SpiceJet flights from Dubai to Amritsar, Jaipur, Mumbai and Delhi had been cancelled on November 12, 2026, due to the carrier owing AED 14 million ($3.8 million).

According to the publication, Dubai Airports, which manages Dubai International Airport (DXB) and Al Maktoum International Airport (DWC), emailed SpiceJet to advise the airline that it had not received payment since October 13, 2026.

Dubai Airports also advised SpiceJet that check-in services would be suspended due to non-adherence to payment conditions, the report said.

Venkat Mangudi / Creative Commons 

According to Flightradar24 data, a SpiceJet flight scheduled from Dubai International to Delhi on November 13, 2026, at 09:50, local time, was cancelled, as was a flight to Mumbai at 12:20.

Further flights on November 13, 2026, to Amritsar and Jaipur have also been cancelled.

A SpiceJet spokesperson told the Hindustan Times that the airline was working with the relevant authorities to rectify the situation.

“We have adequate bank guarantee cover in place and are working to ensure that the issue is sorted out at the earliest,” the spokesperson said.

SpiceJet financial woes

items.t: SpiceJet flights from Dubai cancelled over unpaid airport fees: reports

items.title: Japan could slash F-35 fighter purchases amid defense budget clash
items.summary:
Japan’s Ministry of Finance has proposed a five-year defense budget well below the level that some defense officials had expected.  

Citing four people familiar with the discussions, Reuters reported on November 13, 2026 , that the gap could force cuts of up to 50% to some planned aircraft and missile purchases, including Lockheed Martin F-35 fighters. 

According to the report, Finance Ministry officials proposed spending between 50 trillion and 60 trillion yen ($313 billion to $375 billion) on defense over five years beginning from April 2027.  

That would exceed the approximately 43 trillion yen ($269 billion) allocated under Japan’s current Defense Buildup Program for fiscal years 2023 to 2027. However, it would also fall well short of the roughly 80 trillion yen ($500 billion) that some defense officials and ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) lawmakers had anticipated and used in negotiations with contractors. 

Japanese defense contractors warned of potential order cuts 

According to the sources, Japanese officials have warned defense contractors that expected orders could be cut sharply. Japan’s largest defense manufacturers include Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI), Mitsubishi Electric and Kawasaki Heavy Industries. 

One of the sources suggested that drone purchases could be spared. The Japan Ground Self-Defense Force has been evaluating systems in that category, including Helsing’s HX-2 strike drone . Rakuten previously said field trials of the HX-2 would continue through September 2026. 

According to three of the sources, Finance Ministry officials…
items.t: Japan could slash F-35 fighter purchases amid defense budget clash

items.title: A380 startup Global Airlines ordered into compulsory liquidation by UK court
items.summary:
Airbus A380 startup Global Airlines has been ordered into compulsory liquidation by the Insolvency and Companies Court in the United Kingdom (UK).

On November 12, 2026, The Gazette, an official public record, published a formal notice confirming that the court had granted a ‘Winding-Up Order’ on November 4, 2026. This followed a ‘Petition to Wind Up’ that was filed with the UK court in May 2026.

According to the UK government, individuals can apply to the court to close or wind up a company if it cannot pay its debts, also known as compulsory liquidation.

Since the petition was first made, several hearings have been scheduled over the past few months at the Insolvency and Companies Court. It is understood that the most recent court hearing was held in October 2026.

Global Airlines 

Among those that joined the case as supporting creditors were former Global Airlines company directors Tom Stokely and Prashant Uttamchandani. Both individuals were represented by law firm Katten Muchin Rosenman.

In line with a winding-up order, an officer of the court, known as the ‘Official Receiver’ is put in charge of winding-up the company.

By UK government guidelines, when a company receives a winding-up order its bank account will usually be frozen and its assets or property will be sold by the official receiver.

An application can be made to cancel a winding-up order if the company does not feel that it needs to pay its creditors. This must be done within five working days of getting the order.

On the Companies House website, Global Airlines still shows as an active company.…
items.t: A380 startup Global Airlines ordered into compulsory liquidation by UK court
